title: AIDA implementation ledger
description: The one store for what an implementation run has done, at <task folder>/implementation/ledger.json (ideal/implementation.md, 'The ledger is the state file, not a status log'). It exists so a person who was not watching can arrive afterwards and decide what to redo, and so a run that died mid-order knows where it got to. Plain JSON, no fences, no markdown. Nothing derivable is stored: which orders depend on which lives in the work orders, and which order is in flight is the one order with a step reached, no stop reason and no close, since orders run one at a time. A field present in a real ledger but absent from this schema's `properties` is a defect in the schema, not a value to silently accept, which is why `additionalProperties` is false. This schema holds what exists, never what is planned. The commit range an order produced arrived on 2026-09-11 with `close`, the step that writes it. The checkpoint's own judgements arrived the same day with `tests-freeze`. The stopped state and its three ways out replaced the halts and their five routes in 6.1.0. foundations.md: a new thing gets the least that works, and a field nobody has asked for is a field nobody can cut back.

schemaVersion.description: The shape this file was written in, the same field every other AIDA record carries.

startedFrom.description: The commit the build started from, captured by the first step before anything is written. Rollback is a reset to it, which is what replaces the isolated working copy version 6 decided against. Version 5 captures nothing of the kind and its own ledger needs one. Rewritten by one thing only, `start --rebased-onto <commit>`, after a rebase or an amend left this commit on no branch, or after the branch moved forward onto a later commit before any order committed; the value it replaced is kept under startedFromBefore.

startedAt.description: The UTC time the ledger was opened, set by the first step and kept by every reopening. The one clock the run's `budget.minutes` ceiling in task.json is measured from: what was spent is recomputed from this and the wall clock at each dispatch, and stored nowhere, so nothing a builder writes can reset it.

runMode.description: The mode the build started under: the task's own mode for the implement stage, read through task_run_mode and written by every `start`, new or resumed. It is a record, and no step decides from it. Every step reads task_run_mode itself. Two sources disagreed when a person set the task interactive after a stop: the order left its stop and the ruling after it was refused as unattended (gap row 265). Review reads the task too (nyc defect 20).

snapshotHash.description: The `hash` of the snapshot this ledger was opened against. Reopening compares it to the snapshot on disk and refuses when they disagree, so a ledger and a snapshot that do not belong together are never read as a pair. The failure this prevents is a resumed run recording progress against orders it was not built from.

orders.description: One entry per work order in the snapshot, opened by the first step at no step completed. Order-level state is the thing version 5 records nowhere, which is why a person arriving at one of its runs cannot list which orders finished.

criteria.description: One entry per criterion in the snapshot's contract, opened by the first step as not judged. This holds whether the tests claiming to prove a criterion were confirmed to do so, never the criterion itself, which lives in the snapshot.

startedFromBefore.description: One entry per value startedFrom held before `start --rebased-onto` rewrote it, in the order it happened. Present only when at least one rewrite was. A resumed `start` refuses (exit 82) when HEAD does not descend from startedFrom, because a rebase or an amend left that commit on no branch: `preconditions` would label the baseline with it and `finish` would compute a range git cannot resolve. The rewrite keeps the old value here rather than dropping it, so a reader can tell which commit the baseline on disk was taken at, and why it must be retaken (nyc defect 19).

stopsCleared.description: One entry per time an order left its stopped state, or lost some of its stop reasons, in the order it happened. Present only when at least one was. `go-on`, `redo` and `drop` write one each, the three ways out, each through a person's answer. `review-record --accept-deviation` and `build-record --accept-deviation` write one when a person kept a departure or a deviation the builder declared, removing that reason alone (gap rows 224 and 266). A resumed `start` writes one when its own comparison no longer finds the drift a reason was written for, since `start` is the one action that computes drift (live-run row 143). The reasons removed live on here and nowhere else.

resnapshots.description: One entry per order the snapshot took a live copy of after the first capture, in the order it happened. Present only when at least one was. `start` writes one for a drifted order that had not started, and one for a started or closed order that only gained owned files, findings or an appended reason, which takes its live copy in place (live-run row 91, gap rows 226 and 227). `redo` writes one for the order it takes fresh. Each is written only after design closed on the live copy (live-run row 72). An order is frozen when it starts, not when the stage starts, and this is the record of which shape each order was built from.

setAside.description: One entry per `start` that moved uncommitted files out of the task's tree, in the order it happened. Present only when one did. A role stopped mid-run leaves its files uncommitted, and the next role would work beside them (gap row 217). Unattended, or with `--leftovers set-aside`, `start` moves them under the folder this entry names. Nothing is deleted.

at.description: The UTC time of the move. Set by the script, never typed.

folder.description: The folder the files moved to, under the implementation folder. Each file keeps its path relative to the tree.

path.description: The file's path relative to the tree.

orders.description: The orders whose owned files hold the path. Empty when none does.

id.description: The work order's own id, minted by design. Joined on, never re-minted.

lastStep.description: The last step of this order that finished, or null when none has. A resumed run redoes the step after this one, which is why every step must be safe to run again: the record names what completed, never what was in progress. The order's state derives from this and from `stopped`, and needs no field of its own. Null is planned, `tests-frozen` has its tests frozen, `code-written` and `checks-passed` are built, `reviewed` and `fixed` are in review, `closed` is done, and `dropped` ended without code. An order with a stop reason is stopped, whatever its step.

stopped.description: Why this order stopped, one entry per reason, present only while it is stopped. Absent means the order is not stopped; it is never an empty list, because absent and empty would be one value for two facts. A stopped order refuses every later step (exit 49) until a person takes one of three ways out, `go-on`, `redo` or `drop`, and `finish` refuses while any order is stopped.

attemptsUsed.description: How many times a builder has been given this order. The loop stops on a counter and never on a reviewer being satisfied, so a counter that resets when a run is resumed is not a cap. Version 5 keeps the same count in a crash-atomic sidecar whose header warns never to reset it.

roundsUsed.description: How many fix rounds this order has had. One round is one fixer and one verification. Same reason as attemptsUsed.

lightRounds.description: Present, and true, once `fix-record` has recorded a fix round of this order on a light task. The order's cap then stays one round when a person later sets the task interactive to rule, because the round was spent under that cap (gap row 296).

commitRange.description: The commits this order produced, the first commit of its own build attempt and the code repository's HEAD when it closed, joined by two dots. For an order whose proof is record both commits are the project folder's, where its deliverable landed (nyc defect 17). Written by `close` and by nothing else, so its presence is a second reading of a closed order beside lastStep. In the code repository the left side is the freeze record's commit for this order, so every build attempt is inside (gap row 222). When another order's commit sits between two of this order's attempts, the left side is the last such commit instead, and `close` prints this order's earlier commits beside the range. For an order whose proof is record the left side is the build record's own startedAt. Either way the left side is not the ledger's startedFrom: orders build one after another, so the ledger's value would sweep every earlier order's commits into this one's range, and a range that names work the order did not do is worse than no range at all.

attemptsAllowed.description: How many attempts this order is allowed, present only when a person has granted one beyond the default. Absent means the script's own BUILD_ATTEMPTS_ALLOWED. `go-on --continue build` writes it, one higher than it was, when the attempts are spent, and never lowers it. The grant raises the allowance rather than lowering attemptsUsed, so the count of what a builder already spent stays a fact about the past (ideal/implementation.md, 'What a halt at the attempt cap leads to').

grants.description: One entry per attempt a person has granted on this order through `go-on --continue build`, in the order they were granted. Present only when at least one was. A grant with no record of who asked for what is a cap nobody can audit afterwards.

roundsGranted.description: How many fix rounds a person added to this order's allowance through `go-on --continue fix`, one each time the rounds were spent. Present only when at least one was. roundsUsed never goes down, so the allowance rises instead.

owns.description: The files a person's `go-on --owns` gave this order, beside the ownedFiles the snapshot holds. Present only when one was given. The build brief, the dispatch record, the fix scope and the owned-files check read them as owned. The snapshot keeps design's own list, so `start` compares design with it alone. No other order owns one of these, and none is a frozen test.

redos.description: One entry per time a person redid this order with `redo`, in the order it happened. Present only when one was. Each redo sets the entry back to planned and keeps this list. `tests-brief` hands the newest entry's words to the fresh test author.

dropped.description: Present only on an order a person dropped with `drop`: lastStep is `dropped`. `finish` lists the order and the criteria it leaves unbuilt.

repairs.description: One entry per repair a dependent order opened on this order after it closed, in the order they were opened, and the order's own repair round when it had one. Present only when one was. `build-record` writes it when a builder stops with `Stop: closed-order-defect: <file>: <what fails>` and the file is this order's. It adds one finding to this order's review record, sends the order back to `reviewed` or `fixed`, and adds one fix round to its allowance, so roundsUsed never goes down. The order's fixer repairs it and its reviewer verifies the round, and `close` writes the range again (gap row 286). `reopen` writes one entry per order the same way for the findings of a failed task review (gap row 390).

rowsCarried.description: On a record order a model confirmed: the done-when rows, keyed <order id>:<n>, whose confirmation came from a checker pass before the last one, because their line was unchanged (gap row 361). Absent when the last pass judged every row.

doneWhenJudgement.description: The checkpoint's verdict on the tests that prove this order's own doneWhen rather than a criterion: the `--row` keyed by the order's id, written by `tests-freeze` and replaced on every freeze of this order. Present only when the order froze such a test. A supporting order serves criteria it cannot observe, so its tests are judged against its doneWhen text instead of a verify clause (live-run row 59). Counted with the criterion judgements in every rowsJudgedByModel, so a model's reading here is listed for a person to judge again like any other.

doneWhenGained.description: The done-when rows design appended after this order's tests were frozen, each verbatim. Written by `start` when it takes the live copy in place with the frozen tests kept, on an order at tests-frozen whose done-when row was judged. That judgement read the shorter text, so `start` removes it. `build-brief` and `dispatch-open implementer` refuse while this stands (exit 120). The next freeze with the same tests judges the done-when row again and removes it (gap row 409).

doneWhenGainedAt.description: The UTC time `start` last wrote doneWhenGained. Present only beside it. While it stands, `tests-freeze` refuses (exit 64) unless `implementation/row-check-<order id>.json` holds a verdict on the order's done-when row and was written at or after this time, so a verdict on the shorter text clears nothing. Removed with doneWhenGained (gap row 409).

criterion.description: The row's key: a criterion id, the order id for the done-when row, or `<order id>:absence:<n>` for a routed absence clause, n its done-when row counted from 1 (gap row 273).

personWords.description: The person's words, verbatim, from the row's `--row <key>=rejected::person::<words>` flag. Absent on a row the checker rejected on an unattended run and sent back (gap row 373).

checkerNote.description: The checker's note on this row, read from `implementation/row-check-<order id>.json`. Null when that file or its row is absent.

redAgain.description: The name of every `--test` with a `--red` in a file that holds one of this row's tests. A `--locks-in` test has no red run, so it is not here. The repair edits that file, so each of those red runs is then older than it, and `tests-freeze` refuses it (exit 109). `tests-brief` joins these lists under `rowsRejected.redAgain` (gap row 258).

rowsRejected.description: The rows a person rejected at the checkpoint, written by `tests-freeze` when it refuses on them and replaced on each such refusal. Removed by the next freeze that writes, since that freeze had no rejected row. Present only while one stands. `tests-brief` carries it to a fresh test author, because the person's words otherwise lived only in the conversation (gap row 218). A row the checker rejected on an unattended run is here only when its verdict file marks it `"repair": "tests"` and its key is not yet in rowsSentBack. Any other such row halts the order instead (gap row 373).

rowsSentBack.description: The keys of the rows a checker's rejection sent back to the test author on an unattended run, written by `tests-freeze` beside rowsRejected. A row goes back once: a second rejection of a key here stops the order, because the author could not meet the checker's note and no model settles that (gap row 373). Removed by the next freeze that writes.

criterion.description: The row's key: a criterion id, the order id for the done-when row, or `<order id>:absence:<n>` for a routed absence clause, n its done-when row counted from 1 (gap row 273).

note.description: For a model's row, the checker's own note from `implementation/row-check-<order id>.json` when that file confirms the row. Otherwise the note on the row's `--row` flag.

recordedAt.description: The UTC time the checker's verdict file was last written, when it exists and is older than the refusal. Otherwise the time of the refusal. Set by the script, never typed. The next freeze carries the row only when none of its test files changed after this time.

rowsConfirmed.description: The confirmed rows a freeze held when it refused, with their notes: on exit 65 less the rows its `checkAgain` line names, and on exit 64 for missing rows all of them. Written by `tests-freeze` on each such refusal and replaced by the next one. Removed by the next freeze that writes. A repair round's checker judges only the rows put to it and writes the same verdict file, so these notes are on disk nowhere else. The next freeze carries each one that no `--row` gives (gap row 259).

absenceClauses.description: The doneWhen clauses of this order that assert an absence, each verbatim, written by `tests-freeze --absence` and replaced on every freeze of this order. Present only when the freeze routed at least one. Such a clause cannot be watched failing: the tree is already in the state it asserts, and making a test of it fail means adding the very thing the clause forbids (live-run row 184). It is answered at review instead, where the architecture reviewer judges it against the task's own diff. The list is what makes the route visible: a clause here is owed a verdict, and a clause nobody routed is owed a test.

id.description: The criterion id scope minted. Joined on, never re-minted, and never the criterion's text.

rowState.description: Whether the tests claiming to prove this criterion were confirmed to observe what its verify clause describes. Three values, because unconfirmed reading the same as confirmed is how nobody can tell what is still owed. Opened at not-judged by the first step.

judgements.description: One entry per order whose frozen tests name this criterion, appended by `tests-freeze` when that order's rows are frozen; a serving order whose tests name only its own done-when appends none, and its judgement sits on its ledger entry as doneWhenJudgement. Present only on a criterion a machine verifies: one a person verifies carries a checklist in the frozen test record and never a judgement, and completion confirms it. `close` reads this list to decide rowState.

commit.description: The value startedFrom held before the rewrite.

at.description: The UTC date of the rewrite, YYYY-MM-DD. Set by the script, never typed.

id.description: The order whose live copy the snapshot took.

from.description: The snapshot's hash before the copy was taken.

to.description: The snapshot's hash after, which snapshotHash also became.

at.description: The UTC date the copy was taken, YYYY-MM-DD. Set by the script, never typed.

added.description: Present only when the snapshot did not hold the order before: design added it after the build started, and start took it in, not started (gap row 335). Absent, the entry replaced a copy the snapshot held.

step.description: The step that wrote the reason, such as start, build-record or verify-record.

reason.description: Why the order stopped, in plain words. A step run twice writes no second copy.

allows.description: The go-on choices this reason allows. `go-on` takes a choice only when every reason of the order allows it. An empty list leaves only redo and drop, as for a design change.

id.description: The order whose stop reasons were removed.

by.description: What removed them: one of the three ways out, a person's keep of a deviation, or a resumed start that no longer finds the drift.

reasons.description: The reasons removed, as they stood.

clearedAt.description: The UTC date, YYYY-MM-DD. Set by the script, never typed.

because.description: The person's words, or the script's own account for a start.

owns.description: On a go-on, the files it gave the order.

listed.description: On a go-on that closes, the open findings it ruled deferred with the person's words.

movedTo.description: On a redo or a drop, the dated folder the order's records moved to.

at.description: The UTC date of the redo or the drop, YYYY-MM-DD. Set by the script, never typed.

movedTo.description: The folder the order's records moved to, implementation-<date>-<HEAD> beside the implementation folder, with -<n> when that name was taken. It holds redone.json or dropped.json with the same words. Nothing is deleted.

commit.description: One of the order's own commits, read from its records' commit lists.

reverted.description: The order's own commits, newest first, each with the commit that reverted it. Empty when the tree held none.

by.description: The order whose builder stopped on the defect. It builds again only once this order closes.

attempt.description: The attempt of that order the stop did not spend. Another repair at the same attempt opens only once every earlier one's finding reads addressed, and no more than that order's attempts allowed, so a builder that stops on every run stops the order as any other stop does.

finding.description: The finding the repair added to this order's review record, with origin `repair`.

report.description: The stopped builder's report, which holds the evidence.

at.description: The UTC date the repair opened. Set by the script, never typed.

closedRange.description: The commitRange this order held when the repair reopened it. `close` writes the range again, so this keeps the first one.

commits.description: The commits the stopped builder made after it began. This order's repair round reads them as the stopped order's, not its own, and starts after them (gap row 381).

review.description: The reviewedRange of the failed task review that reopened this order. `reopen` writes it (gap row 390).

reviewFindings.description: The task review's findings this order took: each fails a criterion this order serves, in a file it owns, or a file only it owns.

findings.description: The findings `reopen` added to this order's review record for them, with origin `repair`, in the same order.

at.description: The UTC date the order was reopened. Set by the script, never typed.

closedRange.description: The commitRange this order held when the review reopened it. `close` writes the range again, so this keeps the first one.

round.description: The fix round `fix-brief` opened past a light order's cap, once per order. It adds one round to the allowance (gap row 314).

findings.description: The open findings the round takes: new breakage from the last round, or a finding its fixer reported scope-insufficient that a person widened with --allow.

at.description: The UTC date the round opened. Set by the script, never typed.

reason.description: Why the person granted another attempt, in their own words. Required, because a grant with no reason reads as the cap never having meant anything.

grantedAt.description: The UTC date the grant was made, YYYY-MM-DD. Set by the script, never typed.

allowedAfter.description: What attemptsAllowed became with this grant. Recorded per grant so a reader sees the sequence rather than only the total.

unit.description: The work order whose rows this judgement answers. One order judges one criterion once: a second freeze of the same order replaces its entry rather than adding one, so a row is never counted twice.

verdict.description: Whether these tests observe the part of the verify clause this order is responsible for. A rejected row never reaches this file today, because `tests-freeze` refuses the freeze on one and sends the row back to the test author; the value exists so `close` can derive a rejection rather than assume it away.

judgedBy.description: Who answered. `model` marks a row the row-checker judged, a context that did not write the tests, and that no person re-read. The checker judges every row in both modes against the test-authoring recipe. On an attended run a person answers only a row it rejected, and that answer is `person` (live-run row 70). `person` is refused on an autonomous run. A model's row is weaker evidence than a person's reading, and the record says so rather than marking the row passed. A person returning can then list exactly those rows and judge them again (ideal/implementation.md, 'This departs from the tenth invariant, and says so'). `gate` marks a criterion owned by an order whose proof is gate, written by `close` when the order's configuration-gate check was met on its closing attempt: the recipe's own lines decided it, deterministically. A third value rather than `model`, because a model's row is weaker evidence queued for a person to judge again and this one is not; rather than `person`, because nobody read anything. rowsJudgedByModel never counts it (live-run row 65). A criterion owned by an order whose proof is record is written by `close` from the order's done-when judgement with that row's own judge, `person` or `model`, never `gate`: somebody read the row (nyc defect 17).

note.description: What the judge saw, in their own words. Required with every verdict, because a verdict with nothing to read beside it cannot be re-judged.
